title: Counting an Approval Term on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
The basis on which an approval term is counted on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan is read from the number of fills standing paid on the pharmacy record for the contract year and from whether the prescriber's supporting statement stands received. The plan treats 3 or more fills standing paid as settled therapy.

1. Where the member's fills standing paid on the pharmacy record for the contract year are 3 or more and the prescriber's supporting statement stands received, the term is taken in whole thirty-day supply cycles and rounded down to a whole cycle of 30 days.
2. Where the member's fills standing paid on the pharmacy record for the contract year are fewer than 3 and the prescriber's supporting statement stands received, the term is taken in whole weeks and rounded down to a whole week of 7 days.
3. Where the prescriber's supporting statement does not stand received, the term is counted as booked, whatever the fill history shows.

| Fills standing paid for the contract year | The prescriber's supporting statement | How the term is counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 or more | stands received | in whole cycles of 30 days, rounded down |
| fewer than 3 | stands received | in whole weeks of 7 days, rounded down |
| 3 or more | not received | as booked |
| fewer than 3 | not received | as booked |

A record carrying exactly 3 fills standing paid meets settled therapy; one carrying 2 does not.

## Worked on hypothetical terms

Take a term of 365 days. Counted in whole cycles of 30 days it gives 12 whole cycles and is rounded down to 360 days; counted in whole weeks of 7 days it gives 52 whole weeks and is rounded down to 364 days; counted as booked it stands at 365 days.

Take a term of 90 days. Counted in whole cycles of 30 days it gives 3 whole cycles and stands at 90 days, the rounding taking nothing off; counted in whole weeks it gives 12 whole weeks and is rounded down to 84 days.
